# opencode-limits-go [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/cusvv/opencode-limits-go?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/cusvv/opencode-limits-go/releases/latest) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/cusvv/opencode-limits-go/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=CI)](https://github.com/cusvv/opencode-limits-go/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/opencode-limits-go?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-limits-go) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode-v2.3%2B-111827?style=flat-square)](https://opencode.ai) [![Language](https://img.shields.io/badge/Lang-EN%20%7C%20RU-16a34a?style=flat-square)](#localization) **OpenCode Go** quota monitor plugin for **OpenCode v2.3+** (TUI & Desktop GUI). Live usage across all three OpenCode Go windows — **5-hour rolling**, **weekly**, and **monthly** — with risk verdicts, pace estimation, a 5h trend sparkline, threshold & reset alerts, deep strip/dialog customization, English/Russian localization, and checksum-verified GitHub updates. --- ## Screenshots

Desktop settings dialog

TUI is intentionally one line in the sidebar: ```text 5h ██░░ 42% · 1w █░░░ 31% · 1m ███░ 78% (3d 4h) ``` --- ## Highlights ### Quota & pace intelligence - **All OpenCode Go windows**: `5h` / `1w` / `1m` percentages, reset timestamps, countdowns, recent deltas (`+X%`), and a risk-ranked tightest window. - **Risk verdicts**: each window says whether it will survive until reset, or roughly when it will hit 100%. A 5h window about to reset no longer hides a weekly window that will actually run out first. - **Smart pace & 5h sparkline**: combines window-average and snapshot history to detect coding bursts (`⚡`) and renders a real 5h+ trend inside the dialog. - **OpenCode Zen & today**: active Console budgets (`$spent / $limit`), today's Go tokens / Zen USD spend, top models, and a **last-7-days** slice. - **Reset-aligned cold start**: persists the last valid snapshot for 0 ms startup, refreshes 3 seconds after any window resets, respects `Retry-After` on `429`/`503`, and slows background polling 3× when minimized. ### Alerts that reach you - Threshold toasts (`50%` / `70%` / `80%` / `90%` / `100%`), quota-reset recovery toasts, fast-burn spike alerts, and **"won't survive until reset"** warnings. - **System notifications** when the app is not focused — **off by default**, opt-in, and only for 100% quota (max once per 10 minutes). In-app toasts remain separate. - Alerts are deduplicated per account/window/reset, persisted in TUI storage across `/reload`, and never fire on stale disk-cache data. ### Deep customization - **Desktop GUI**: window selection, auto-focus, auto-hide below `50%` / `70%` / `80%`, four bar palettes, three densities, indicator styles (`Bar + %`, text, bars), remaining-% mode, reset countdown modes, 24h/12h clocks, per-block dialog toggles. - **TUI**: bars, remaining-% mode, window filter, alert threshold, fast-burn sensitivity, mute, hide-strip, plain ASCII, language override, and persisted alert state. - **GUI ↔ TUI sync**: window filters, `% left`, alerts, thresholds, burn-spike sensitivity, and language sync via plugin RPC (or `options` in `opencode.json`). ### Credentials and updates - Works with OpenCode Console **OAuth** (`opencode`), saved **API keys** (`opencode-go` / `opencode`), env vars (`OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY`), plugin options, `opencode auth export`, and legacy `auth.json`. - Tokens never leave the server process — never sent over RPC, never shown in the UI, and redacted from logs. - **Dev installs (`git clone` or `local-plugins`) are never overwritten** by the updater. Release installs update only from a release that ships `SHA256SUMS`, with a version check, fail-closed archive-listing preflight, an owner-token process lock, size caps, and `package.json` written last. The update check cache is still honored for dev and package-manager installs (they are never auto-installed). --- ## Installation Requires **OpenCode v2.3.0+**, an active OpenCode Go credential (`opencode auth login` or `OPENCODE_API_KEY`), and **Node.js >= 20** for the server and Desktop GUI. The optional TUI entrypoint depends on `@opentui/core` and inherits its engines: **Node >= 26.4 or Bun >= 1.3.14**. CI runs on Node 24 to typecheck, test, and build, and does not execute the TUI runtime. ### Option 1: OpenCode CLI (recommended) ```sh opencode plugin add opencode-limits-go # or directly from GitHub: opencode plugin add github:cusvv/opencode-limits-go ``` Restart **OpenCode Desktop** (or run `/reload` in open TUI sessions). ### Option 2: Clone with Git ```sh # macOS / Linux git clone https://github.com/cusvv/opencode-limits-go.git ~/.config/opencode/local-plugins/opencode-limits-go cd ~/.config/opencode/local-plugins/opencode-limits-go && npm install ``` ```powershell # Windows (PowerShell) git clone https://github.com/cusvv/opencode-limits-go.git "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\opencode\local-plugins\opencode-limits-go" cd "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\opencode\local-plugins\opencode-limits-go"; npm install ``` `npm install` is required for the TUI entrypoint (`solid-js` and `@opentui/solid`). The Desktop GUI bundle is prebuilt. Server and Desktop need Node >= 20; the TUI runtime additionally requires `@opentui/core` engines (Node >= 26.4 or Bun >= 1.3.14). ### Option 3: Release archive Download `opencode-limits-go.zip` or `opencode-limits-go.tar.gz` plus `SHA256SUMS` from [Releases](https://github.com/cusvv/opencode-limits-go/releases), verify with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` (Windows: `certutil -hashfile opencode-limits-go.zip SHA256`), and extract to: - **Windows**: `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\local-plugins\opencode-limits-go` - **macOS / Linux**: `~/.config/opencode/local-plugins/opencode-limits-go` Then run `npm install` in that directory, as for the git clone. ### Enable in `opencode.json` (Options 2 & 3) Add `./local-plugins/opencode-limits-go` to `plugins` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\opencode.json`): ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": [ "./local-plugins/opencode-limits-go" ] } ``` Optional defaults: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "./local-plugins/opencode-limits-go", "options": { "token": "{env:OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY}", "showRemaining": false, "warnThreshold": 80, "burnSpikePct": 20, "langOverride": "auto", "autoUpdate": true } } ] } ``` Restart **OpenCode Desktop** and run `/reload` in open TUI sessions. --- ## Usage & shortcuts | Action | Shortcut / command | |---|---| | Show limits dialog / popup | `/limits` or `Ctrl+Shift+L` (or click the status strip in Desktop) | | Quick settings | `/limits-settings`, gear button in Desktop, or **Settings → OpenCode Go limits** | | Filter TUI sidebar windows | `/limits-windows` | The TUI keybind can be rebound in OpenCode's keymap; `/limits` always works. ### Desktop vs TUI | Capability | Desktop GUI | TUI | |---|---|---| | Three windows, pace, sparkline, Zen stats | Yes | Yes (popup) | | System notifications | Yes | Yes | | Bars / remaining % / window filter | Yes | Yes | | Alert threshold / burn-spike / mute | Yes | Yes | | Hide strip / plain ASCII | Placement **Hidden** | Settings | | Palettes, density, auto-hide, 12h clock | Yes | No (24h only) | | Settings sync with the other UI | Yes | Yes | ### Defaults | Setting | Default | |---|---| | Placement (Desktop) | Bottom strip, always visible | | TUI strip | All three windows, text only, visible | | Poll interval | 90s (3× slower when Desktop is minimized) | | Alert threshold | 80% and 100% | | System notifications | Off; when enabled, 100% only, max once per 10 min | | Fast-burn spike | +20% in 5–30 min | | Auto-update | On for release installs; ignored for git/`local-plugins` installs | | Language | Follow OpenCode UI (TUI falls back to `OPENCODE_LANG`/`LC_ALL`/`LANG`) | ### Verify via CLI ```sh opencode plugin list opencode api post /api/rpc/opencode-limits-go/status --data '{"input":{"force":true}}' ``` A healthy response has `"ok": true` and a non-empty `rows` array with language-neutral values (`label`: `5h`/`1w`/`1m`, `resetsIn`: `""` or `"?"`). A failure has `"ok": false` and an authoritative machine-readable `errorCode` (`NO_TOKEN`, `AUTH`, `RATE_LIMIT`, `OFFLINE`, `BAD_RESPONSE`, `CREDENTIALS_CHANGED`, `INTERNAL`); the legacy `error` field repeats that code. `lang` is deprecated and ignored — the UI localizes the card on render. Example: ```json { "ok": false, "errorCode": "AUTH", "error": "AUTH", "errorDetail": "HTTP 401: invalid token", "tight": "" } ``` --- ## Troubleshooting **Plugin not listed in `opencode plugin list`** - Check the `plugins` entry and restart the app. Local installs must point at the directory containing `package.json`. - Run `npm install` in the plugin directory if the TUI strip never appears but Desktop works. **`NO_TOKEN` / `401` / `403`** - Run `opencode auth login`, or set `OPENCODE_API_KEY` / `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` and restart. - In Desktop, the error dialog has **Copy login cmd**, **Console**, and **Retry**. **Offline / `429` / `503`** - The last good snapshot is shown with a stale marker and its age. The plugin honors `Retry-After` and backs off; no action is usually needed. **Logs and diagnostics** - Log: `%TEMP%\opencode-limits-go\limits.log` (Windows) or `/tmp/opencode-limits-go/limits.log` (macOS/Linux). - Desktop settings include **Diagnostics → Copy info** with version, source, usage, and placement (no tokens). **Uninstall** - `opencode plugin remove opencode-limits-go`, or remove the `plugins` entry and delete the plugin directory. --- ## Security - No telemetry. Network access is limited to the OpenCode Go usage endpoint and GitHub releases. - Tokens are read server-side and never cross RPC. Credential lookup is time-bounded, and Windows CLI fallback blocks current-directory executable hijacking. - Logs are created in a private directory (`0700`) with `0600` files and redact bearer/basic tokens, JWTs, JSON secret values, auth headers, and common API-key formats. - Updates require HTTPS GitHub hosts, `SHA256SUMS`, a matching `package.json` version, a fail-closed archive listing check, and a stale-aware process lock with an owner token. Dev/git installs are excluded. --- ## Localization Follows your OpenCode UI language (**English** / **Russian**), or can be overridden manually (`Auto` / `EN` / `RU`) in **Settings → Behavior & language** (Desktop) or TUI settings. --- ## Development ```sh npm install npm test # core + server + ui-state + present tests (contract, parity, alerts) npm run build # typecheck server/TUI/GUI and rebuild dist/gui-experimental.cjs ``` CI uses Node 24 on Linux, Windows, and macOS. It typechecks/tests/builds the plugin but does not launch the TUI runtime; local TUI use must satisfy `@opentui/core` engines (Node >= 26.4 or Bun >= 1.3.14). ### Project architecture ```text src/ index.ts Wiring: plugin setup, RPC handlers, timers rpc.ts / rpc/ Portable RPC contract (status, prefs, updates, diagnostics, events) gui.tsx, tui.tsx Desktop/TUI entrypoints gui/, tui/ Presentation only (Solid GUI modules, terminal UI modules) core/ Domain: types, parsing, window risk, pace, alert detection, stats present/ Copy/format: labels, durations, errors, alerts, verdicts, TUI text i18n/ EN/RU dictionaries, typed keys, parity ui-state/ Single-flight poller, alert reducer, shared-pref application settings/ Shared prefs schema, defaults, sanitize, merge server/ api.ts OpenCode Go HTTP client with Retry-After log.ts Private rotating JSON logger platform.ts Platform helpers (signals, paths) service/ Cache, history, identity, prefs, status, events, storage credentials/ auth facade + identity/resolver/sources updater/ Checksum-verified GitHub release check, install, rollback dist/ gui-experimental.cjs Prebuilt CommonJS Desktop GUI bundle ``` --- ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

# SPEC — opencode-limits-go

## Purpose

OpenCode v2.3+ plugin (Node >= 20) showing OpenCode Go quota (5h / 1w / 1m) in Desktop GUI and TUI, with pace, risk verdicts, alerts, and OpenCode Zen/today stats. Cards are language-neutral; UIs localize on render.

## Layers

- `src/core/` — domain: types, parsing, window risk math, pace, alert detectors, stats. No Node, IO, or user copy.
- `src/present/` — copy and formatting: labels, durations, errors, alert/verdict/pace strings, TUI sidebar/detail.
- `src/i18n/` — EN/RU dictionaries, typed keys, `message()`; EN/RU parity.
- `src/ui-state/` — framework-agnostic single-flight poller, alert reducer, shared-pref application.
- `src/settings/` — one shared prefs schema, defaults, sanitize, merge.
- `src/rpc/` — RPC contract (`src/rpc.ts` re-exports it); only server↔UI boundary.
- `src/server/service/` — cache, history, identity, prefs, status, events, storage.
- `src/server/credentials/` — `auth.ts` facade + identity/resolver/sources.
- `src/server/updater/` — release check, archive validation, install/rollback.
- `src/server/api.ts`, `log.ts`, `platform.ts` — HTTP, logging, platform helpers.
- `src/gui/`, `src/tui/` — presentation only; `src/index.ts` — wiring, timers, RPC handlers.

## Contract

- `status` returns a language-neutral `LimitCard`:
  - rows: `label` = `5h|1w|1m`, `resetsAt` = numeric date or `"?"`, `resetsIn` = `""`/`"?"`, with `key`/`resetsAtMs` additive;
  - `tight` = `""` (deprecated, UI computes risk);
  - `error` = deprecated machine code, equal to `errorCode`; `errorCode`/`errorDetail` are authoritative (detail is technical, never UI copy);
  - `lang` input is deprecated and ignored;
  - `accountId` = stable HMAC credential fingerprint; `revision` = credential epoch.
- Events: `changed {reason: credentials|reset|usage, accountId?, revision?}`, `updated {version}`, `prefsChanged {prefs, autoUpdate}`.
- `getPrefs`/`setPrefs` exchange shared prefs; `diagnostics` exposes cache/history/prefs/updater summary, never secrets.

## Quota windows

- Risk ranks by projected usage at reset (`used / elapsedRatio`), not raw percent.
- `windowVerdict` returns `exhausted | tight | fits`; UI shows actionable verdicts only.
- Hot pace needs `projectedPct >= 105` and `timeToFull < remaining`; `limited` is exhausted regardless of reported percent.
- Early-window pace is suppressed until 1% elapsed and `used >= 35`; recent snapshot bursts can override the average.

## Cache and accounts

- `lastGood:v1` is row-validated on load; invalid entries are dropped.
- Credential/config events clear disk cache via storage `remove` or a sentinel fallback, so an old account is never shown as current.
- `history:v2` stores snapshots with per-window `resets`; snapshots from another reset are ignored for delta/spike.
- History is tagged with `accountId`; changing account clears it. Alerts are keyed by account + window + reset.
- The server retries when the credential epoch changes and never returns the old account's success.

## Settings

- `src/settings/prefs.ts` is the single schema/defaults/sanitize/merge source.
- Shared prefs priority: storage > plugin options > defaults.
- `autoUpdate` is server-owned with options > storage — an intentional exception to the shared-prefs order.
- A failed pref push shows an error and pulls the server value back; UI never silently keeps a rejected value.
- GUI-only prefs: palette, density, placement, time/reset format, dialog toggles, poll interval.

## Alerts

- One reducer (`ui-state/alerts.ts`) for GUI and TUI; texts come from `present`.
- Persistence is per surface: TUI storage, GUI store; account change clears state.
- Stale cards and disabled alerts do not mutate dedupe state.
- Threshold/reset/spike/risk alerts are in-app toasts. OS notifications are opt-in, 100%-only, and throttled to one per 10 minutes.

## Polling

- Single-flight requests; forced refreshes are queued and coalesced.
- `seq` guards drop stale results; `invalidate()` aborts and resolves waiters; 30s client timeout.
- Credential change invalidates, clears card/zen state, resets the poller, and forces a reload.

## Credentials, updates, logging

- Credentials are server-side only, never over RPC/UI, and redacted in logs (Bearer/Basic/JWT/prefixed keys/headers/JSON secrets).
- Resolution is bounded (8s host hooks, 8s CLI) under a 25s `status` deadline. CLI export is cached 10 minutes single-flight; `dropCli` clears cache and in-flight probe.
- Windows CLI fallback uses `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1` and a home cwd. 429/5xx are token-specific.
- Dev/`local-plugins` installs are never overwritten; package-manager installs defer to `opencode plugin update`.
- Release installs require HTTPS GitHub allowlist, `SHA256SUMS`, matching archive version, owner-token lock, fail-closed listing preflight, size caps, `package.json` copied last, and rollback. Check cache is honored for dev/PM installs.
- Logs: private `0700` dir, `0600` file, `O_NOFOLLOW` where available, 256 KB rotation, write failures ignored.

## UI behavior

- GUI and TUI share thresholds 50/70/80/90/100; `0` disables the warning level and keeps 100.
- All user copy comes from `i18n`/`present`; UI never renders a machine error code as a sentence (`cardErrorText`).
- Strip is a native button with `aria-label`; toggles use `aria-pressed`; sparkline uses `role="img"`.
- TUI strip is compact below 76 columns, hideable, plain-ASCII capable, and resize-reactive.
- Destructive resets require confirmation; Desktop settings search indexes every visible setting.

## Testing

- `npm test` runs core/server/ui-state/present (129 tests): parsing, risk/pace, alerts/history, auth sources + CLI cache, redaction, HTTP retry, updater checksums/listing/lock/rollback/dev guards, RPC contract, EN/RU parity.
- `npm run build` typechecks both tsconfigs and regenerates `dist/gui-experimental.cjs`; CI runs on Linux/Windows/macOS and asserts the bundle is current on Linux.

## Known limits

- No account switcher: only the first working credential is shown; multi-account is guarded in cache/history/alerts.
- The updater verifies a SHA-256 manifest, not a cryptographic signature.
- Runtime requirements differ: server + Desktop GUI need Node >= 20; the optional TUI entrypoint inherits `@opentui/core` engines (Node >= 26.4 or Bun >= 1.3.14) and needs `npm install` (`solid-js`/`@opentui/solid`). CI builds/tests on Node 24 without running TUI.
- RPC exposure and auth are controlled by the OpenCode host.
